html:
SMTO-K8S-0001 — SMTO couldn't read the Kubernetes cluster or namespace name

GUID: f7ebd1ff-29f3-4891-8d57-b95716e8356a
Slug: kubernetes-target-invalid
Domain: K8S · Subsystem: k8s

What happened

  • SMTO tried to note which Kubernetes cluster and namespace (a named group inside the cluster) a command used, but a name or address in your Kubernetes settings isn't valid. The command wasn't blocked; SMTO just won't remember this cluster.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you named a namespace, use only lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, up to 63 characters, starting and ending with a letter or number. Namespace names with capitals, spaces or other symbols are refused.
  2. Ask the person who set up Kubernetes access on the Gateway's computer to check the cluster, context and namespace names and the cluster address in its Kubernetes settings file. SMTO reads those names from that file, and an empty or garbled entry causes this error.
  3. After the names are fixed, ask the agent to run a read-only command such as kubectl get pods. A successful read-only command lets SMTO record the cluster without changing anything.

What success looks like

  • The read-only command succeeds and later Kubernetes steps in the conversation use the same cluster and namespace.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages Kubernetes access. Don't rerun commands that change the cluster just to test this; they already ran.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Kubernetes setup validation rejected an empty or unsafe context, cluster or namespace name, a namespace that is not a lowercase DNS label, a non-string cluster server, or an invalid tls-server-name in the kubeconfig.

What this means

  • Public setup validation rejects a missing/unsafe target name or invalid namespace, or kubeconfig resolution finds a non-string endpoint or invalid TLS server name. These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.

Why this can happen

  • Public setup validation rejects a missing/unsafe target name or invalid namespace, or kubeconfig resolution finds a non-string endpoint or invalid TLS server name.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact context, namespace, endpoint and tls-server-name field named by the producer.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the kubeconfig the Gateway uses (--kubeconfig, KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config on that node): the selected context, its cluster and namespace must be non-empty printable names, the namespace a lowercase DNS label of at most 63 characters, clusters[].cluster.server a string URL, and tls-server-name a valid host name. Then confirm with a read-only kubectl get.
  • Correct the named context/namespace and intended HTTPS endpoint in kubeconfig, then verify the selected target before submitting work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Discovery returns a valid public setup for the intended cluster and namespace.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
